import z from 'zod'

export const printModeErrorSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('error'),
  message: z.string(),
})
export type PrintModeError = z.infer<typeof printModeErrorSchema>

export const printModeDownloadStatusSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('download'),
  version: z.string(),
  status: z.enum(['complete', 'failed']),
})
export type PrintModeDownloadStatus = z.infer<
  typeof printModeDownloadStatusSchema
>

export const printModeToolCallSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('tool_call'),
  toolCallId: z.string(),
  toolName: z.string(),
  args: z.record(z.string(), z.any()),
})
export type PrintModeToolCall = z.infer<typeof printModeToolCallSchema>

export const printModeToolResultSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('tool_result'),
  toolCallId: z.string(),
  result: z.string(),
})
export type PrintModeToolResult = z.infer<typeof printModeToolResultSchema>

export const printModeTextSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('text'),
  text: z.string(),
})
export type PrintModeText = z.infer<typeof printModeTextSchema>

export const printModeFinishSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('finish'),
  agentId: z.string().optional(),
  totalCost: z.number(),
})
export type PrintModeFinish = z.infer<typeof printModeFinishSchema>

export const printModeEventSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  printModeErrorSchema,
  printModeDownloadStatusSchema,
  printModeFinishSchema,
  printModeTextSchema,
  printModeToolCallSchema,
  printModeToolResultSchema,
])

export type PrintModeEvent = z.infer<typeof printModeEventSchema>

import { z } from 'zod'

import { costModes } from './constants'
import { GrantTypeValues } from './types/grant'
import { printModeEventSchema } from './types/print-mode'
import {
  SessionStateSchema,
  toolCallSchema,
  toolResultSchema,
} from './types/session-state'
import { ProjectFileContextSchema } from './util/file'

export const FileChangeSchema = z.object({
  type: z.enum(['patch', 'file']),
  path: z.string(),
  content: z.string(),
})
export type FileChange = z.infer<typeof FileChangeSchema>
export const CHANGES = z.array(FileChangeSchema)
export type FileChanges = z.infer<typeof CHANGES>

export const CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('prompt'),
    promptId: z.string(),
    prompt: z.string().or(z.undefined()),
    promptParams: z.record(z.string(), z.any()).optional(), // Additional json params.
    fingerprintId: z.string(),
    authToken: z.string().optional(),
    costMode: z.enum(costModes).optional().default('normal'),
    sessionState: SessionStateSchema,
    toolResults: z.array(toolResultSchema),
    model: z.string().optional(),
    repoUrl: z.string().optional(),
    agentId: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('read-files-response'),
    files: z.record(z.string(), z.union([z.string(), z.null()])),
    requestId: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('init'),
    fingerprintId: z.string(),
    authToken: z.string().optional(),
    fileContext: ProjectFileContextSchema,
    repoUrl: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('tool-call-response'),
    requestId: z.string(),
    success: z.boolean(),
    result: z.any().optional(), // Tool execution result
    error: z.string().optional(), // Error message if execution failed
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('cancel-user-input'),
    authToken: z.string(),
    promptId: z.string(),
  }),
])

export type ClientAction = z.infer<typeof CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA>

export const UsageReponseSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('usage-response'),
  usage: z.number(),
  remainingBalance: z.number(),
  balanceBreakdown: z
    .record(
      z.enum([GrantTypeValues[0], ...GrantTypeValues.slice(1)]),
      z.number(),
    )
    .optional(),
  next_quota_reset: z.coerce.date().nullable(),
  autoTopupAdded: z.number().optional(),
})
export type UsageResponse = z.infer<typeof UsageReponseSchema>

export const InitResponseSchema = z
  .object({
    type: z.literal('init-response'),
    message: z.string().optional(),
    agentNames: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional(),
  })
  .merge(
    UsageReponseSchema.omit({
      type: true,
    }),
  )
export type InitResponse = z.infer<typeof InitResponseSchema>

export const MessageCostResponseSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('message-cost-response'),
  promptId: z.string(),
  credits: z.number(),
})
export type MessageCostResponse = z.infer<typeof MessageCostResponseSchema>

export const PromptResponseSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('prompt-response'),
  promptId: z.string(),
  sessionState: SessionStateSchema,
  toolCalls: z.array(toolCallSchema),
  toolResults: z.array(toolResultSchema),
})
export type PromptResponse = z.infer<typeof PromptResponseSchema>

export const SERVER_ACTION_SCHEMA = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('response-chunk'),
    userInputId: z.string(),
    chunk: z.union([z.string(), printModeEventSchema]),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('subagent-response-chunk'),
    userInputId: z.string(),
    agentId: z.string(),
    agentType: z.string(),
    chunk: z.string(),
    prompt: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  PromptResponseSchema,
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('read-files'),
    filePaths: z.array(z.string()),
    requestId: z.string(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('tool-call-request'),
    userInputId: z.string(),
    requestId: z.string(),
    toolName: z.string(),
    args: z.record(z.any()),
    timeout: z.number().optional(),
  }),
  InitResponseSchema,
  UsageReponseSchema,
  MessageCostResponseSchema,
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('action-error'),
    message: z.string(),
    error: z.string().optional(),
    remainingBalance: z.number().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    // The server is imminently going to shutdown, and the client should reconnect
    type: z.literal('request-reconnect'),
  }),
])

export type ServerAction = z.infer<typeof SERVER_ACTION_SCHEMA>

**Key Observations:**

3. **Relationship**: `userInputId` appears to be what the server calls the prompt on the backend, while `promptId` is the client-generated identifier. They're likely the same value or have a 1:1 mapping.

**Storage Strategy Insights:**

1. **Use `promptId` as the key** - This is what the client controls and generates, making it the natural choice for client-side storage. The client already uses `promptId` for tracking promise resolvers.

2. **Map vs Record** - A `Map<string, (event: PrintModeEvent) => void>` is cleaner than a plain object for dynamic keys and provides better type safety.

3. **Cleanup consideration** - Need to remove handlers after the prompt completes (in `handlePromptResponse`) to prevent memory leaks.

4. **userInputId matching** - When a `response-chunk` arrives with `userInputId`, we'll need to match it to the stored `promptId`. This means either:

   - Maintaining a separate mapping if they differ

**Edge Cases:**
- Multiple runs in parallel with different promptIds
- Handler called after prompt already completed
- userInputId not matching any known promptId (error case)

**Recommendation**: Store handlers in `Map<string, (event: PrintModeEvent) => void>` keyed by `promptId`, then use `userInputId` directly to look up handlers when chunks arrive (assuming they're the same).

Looking at the current `CodebuffClient.run()` method signature, `handleEvent` is a required parameter. To make it optional while maintaining backward compatibility:

## Key Insights

**1. Optional Parameter Typing**
- Change signature from `handleEvent: (event: any) => void` to `handleEvent?: (event: any) => void`
- Users who don't provide it get undefined, which is fine - just don't call it
- No breaking changes: existing code with handleEvent continues working unchanged

**2. Storage Consideration**
- Currently `handleEvent` is passed to `run()` but never actually used or stored anywhere in the codebase
- The parameter exists in the signature but isn't referenced in the method body
- This suggests it may be a placeholder or the feature isn't fully implemented yet

**3. Backward Compatibility Strategy**
- Since the current code doesn't actually use `handleEvent`, making it optional is purely additive
- No existing behavior to preserve - the function currently does nothing with the parameter
- Users who don't pass it: no change in behavior (it was already being ignored)
- Users who do pass it: we need to actually implement the feature now

**4. Implementation Pattern**
- Store handlers in a Map keyed by promptId (which is already generated in `run()`)
- When storing: `if (handleEvent) { this.eventHandlers.set(promptId, handleEvent) }`
- When calling: `const handler = this.eventHandlers.get(promptId); if (handler) { handler(event) }`
- Cleanup: delete handler from Map after prompt completes (in `handlePromptResponse`)

**5. Edge Cases**
- Multiple concurrent runs: each needs its own handler, hence Map by promptId
- Handler cleanup: must remove from Map to avoid memory leaks
- Race conditions: handler should be stored before `sendInput()` call to avoid missing early events

**6. Type Safety**
- Keep parameter as `(event: any) => void` for now, or change to `(event: PrintModeEvent) => void` for stricter typing
- The `any` type provides flexibility if event structure evolves
- PrintModeEvent typing requires importing from common package

The simplest approach: make parameter optional with `?`, store in Map if provided, call if exists when processing chunks, clean up on completion.

Create an Agent Store web interface that allows users to browse and discover published AI agents.

## Core Components Required:

### 1. Agent Store Page
Create a page at `/agents` that displays a grid of available agents with the following features:
- Responsive grid layout showing agent cards (1 column mobile, 2 medium, 3 large screens)
- Search functionality to filter agents by name, description, or tags
- Sort dropdown with options: "Most Used", "Newest", "Name", "Total Spent"
- Loading state with skeleton placeholders
- Empty state when no agents match search criteria
- Smooth animations for card hover effects and layout changes

### 2. Agent Cards
Each agent card should display:
- Agent name and publisher information with verification badge
- Description (truncated to 2 lines)
- Usage statistics in a 2x2 grid showing:
  - Usage count (formatted: 1K, 1M, etc.)
  - Total spent (currency format)
  - Cost per invocation (currency format)
  - Version badge
- Up to 3 tags with "+N" indicator for additional tags
- Hover effects with subtle lift animation
- Clickable links to individual agent pages at `/publishers/{publisherId}/agents/{agentId}/{version}`

### 3. API Endpoint
Create a `/api/agents` GET endpoint that:
- Fetches agent configurations from database with publisher information
- Joins agent_config and publisher tables
- Returns only the latest version of each unique agent
- Includes mock usage metrics (usage_count, total_spent, avg_cost_per_invocation, avg_response_time)
- Parses agent data JSON to extract name, description, and tags
- Limits results to 100 agents for performance
- Orders by creation date (newest first)
- Handles errors gracefully with proper status codes

### 4. Navigation Integration
Update the main navigation to include:
- "Agent Store" link in desktop navigation menu
- "Agent Store" item with Bot icon in mobile dropdown menu
- Proper hover states matching existing navigation styling

### 5. Code Cleanup
Remove unused imports from the CLI agents handler:
- Remove imports for `startAgentCreationChat` and `createAgentFromRequirements` from './agent-creation-chat'

## Technical Requirements:
- Use React Query for data fetching with proper loading states
- Implement proper TypeScript interfaces for agent data
- Use Framer Motion for animations
- Include proper accessibility features
- Handle responsive design breakpoints
- Format numbers and currency appropriately
- Use proper semantic HTML structure

### API Routes Structure Analysis

The codebase uses Next.js App Router for API routes, primarily under `web/src/app/api/`. No routes found in `web/pages/api` (likely Pages Router not in use). These files define RESTful endpoints for user management, referrals, agents, API keys, billing, and more. They interact with a Drizzle ORM schema for database operations, revealing schema structure via imports and queries.

**Relevant Files and Utility:**

- **web/src/app/api/referrals/route.ts**: Core referral API (GET/POST for fetching/redeeming codes). Useful for understanding user/referral schema interactions (e.g., `schema.user`, `schema.referral` fields like `id`, `referral_code`, `credits`); shows authentication with NextAuth.

- **web/src/app/api/referrals/[code]/route.ts**: Dynamic route for validating referral codes (GET). Reveals schema queries on `schema.user` (e.g., `referral_code`, `name`); highlights referral status logic tied to DB constraints.

- **web/src/app/api/referrals/helpers.ts**: Helper for referral redemption logic. Exposes full referral flow with schema (`schema.referral`: `referrer_id`, `referred_id`, `status`, `credits`); includes transaction handling and credit granting, linking to billing schema.

- **web/src/app/api/user/auto-topup/route.ts**: Manages user auto-topup settings (POST). Defines `schema.user` fields (e.g., `auto_topup_enabled`, `auto_topup_threshold`, `auto_topup_amount`); useful for user profile schema and validation.

- **web/src/app/api/user/profile/route.ts**: Fetches user profile (GET). Queries `schema.user` (e.g., `handle`, `referral_code`, `created_at`); integrates auto-topup validation, showing schema extensions.

- **web/src/app/api/agents/[publisherId]/[agentId]/latest/route.ts**: Retrieves latest agent config (GET). Interacts with `schema.publisher`, `schema.agentConfig` (e.g., `id`, `version`, `publisher_id`, `data`); illustrates versioning and org-based schema.

- **web/src/app/api/agents/[publisherId]/[agentId]/[version]/route.ts**: Specific agent version retrieval (GET). Similar to above; queries `schema.agentConfig` with version matching, revealing schema for agent data storage.

- **web/src/app/api/agents/publish/route.ts**: Publishes agent templates (POST). Comprehensive: validates/persists to `schema.agentConfig`; ties into `schema.publisher`, `schema.org`, `schema.orgMember` for permissions; exposes full agent publishing schema.

- **web/src/app/api/api-keys/route.ts**: Manages API keys (GET/POST). Uses `encryptedApiKeys` table (fields: `type`, `user_id`); links to `schema.session` for auth; shows key encryption and storage schema.

- **web/src/app/api/stripe/buy-credits/route.ts**: Handles credit purchases (POST). Queries `schema.user` (e.g., `stripe_customer_id`); integrates with billing (credits in `schema` implied); useful for purchase/credit grant schema flows.

**Database Schema Insights**: Inferred from Drizzle imports (`@codebuff/common/db/schema`). Key tables: `user` (id, name, email, handle, referral_code, auto_topup_*, stripe_customer_id), `referral` (referrer_id, referred_id, credits, status), `agentConfig` (id, version, publisher_id, data), `publisher` (id, user_id, org_id), `org`/`orgMember` (roles, permissions), `encryptedApiKeys` (user_id, type), `session` (sessionToken, userId). Schema supports auth, billing, referrals, and agent management; no full schema file directly, but queries reveal structure. For deeper schema, check `@codebuff/common/db/schema.ts`.

### Relevant Files for Database Schema (Agent Config and Publisher Tables)

- **common/src/db/schema.ts**  
  Core Drizzle ORM schema definitions; directly defines `publisher` and `agent_config` tables with columns, relationships (e.g., to `user` and `org`), enums (e.g., `orgRoleEnum`), indexes, and constraints. Essential for understanding table structure, versioning (major/minor/patch), and data storage for agents/publishers.

### Supporting Files for Schema Usage in API Routes

- **web/src/app/api/publishers/route.ts**  
  API endpoint for GET/POST on publishers; queries `publisher` table via Drizzle, joins with `org` and `org_member` for access checks. Shows how schema integrates with authentication and CRUD operations.

- **web/src/app/api/agents/[publisherId]/[agentId]/latest/route.ts**  
  Retrieves latest `agent_config` version; queries by `publisher_id`, `id`, sorted by semantic version fields. Illustrates schema querying for agent retrieval and versioning logic.

- **web/src/app/api/agents/[publisherId]/[agentId]/[version]/route.ts**  
  Fetches specific `agent_config` version; similar to above but filters by exact `version`. Demonstrates precise schema access for versioned agent data.

- **web/src/app/api/agents/publish/route.ts**  
  Handles publishing agents; validates and inserts into `agent_config` with `publisher_id`, enforces version uniqueness and permissions via schema joins. Key for schema in write operations and constraints.

These files reveal the schema's role in API structure: schema.ts as foundation, routes as entry points using Drizzle for queries/inserts tied to auth and validation.

### Relevant Files for Existing API Patterns and Database Query Examples

These files exemplify Next.js API route structures (e.g., GET/POST handlers with authentication via next-auth, error handling, and JSON responses) and common database patterns using Drizzle ORM (e.g., selects with joins/eq/and, inserts, transactions, schema references). They reference shared schema in `@codebuff/common/db/schema`, aiding schema inference.

- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/route.ts**: Core org CRUD routes; shows auth checks, complex joins for membership/queries, usage calculations—ideal for route structure and query patterns.
- **web/src/app/api/git-evals/route.ts**: POST/GET for eval results; demonstrates insert/returning, conditional queries (admin vs. public), limit/ordering—useful for data persistence examples.
- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/members/route.ts**: Members management; illustrates permission checks, user lookups, transactions for inserts/counts—highlights org-specific query flows.
- **web/src/app/api/publishers/route.ts**: Publisher creation/retrieval; includes validation, complex where clauses with or/and, joins for access control—shows multi-table query patterns.
- **web/src/app/api/api-keys/route.ts**: Key storage; uses Zod parsing, session queries via token—exemplifies secure API patterns with DB encryption.
- **backend/src/api/usage.ts**: Express-style usage handler; Zod validation, auth token resolution, fallback logic—complements web API with backend integration examples.

These cover ~80% of typical patterns; schema details emerge from import `* as schema from '@codebuff/common/db/schema'` across files, suggesting centralized tables like org, user, orgMember.

### Relevant Files for Main Navigation Components and Layout Files

- **web/src/app/layout.tsx**: Root Next.js layout; defines overall app structure including Navbar integration, providers (Theme, Session, Query), and Footer placement—essential for understanding high-level navigation flow and page wrapping.

### Relevant Files for Existing Page Components and Routing Structure

- **web/src/app/layout.tsx**: Root layout component; defines overall app structure with Navbar (navigation links to /docs, /pricing, /usage) and Footer; useful for understanding global routing wrapper and session/providers integration in Next.js App Router.

- **web/src/app/page.tsx**: Home page component (/ route); imports and renders landing UI elements (Hero, FeatureSection, etc.); shows client-side routing hooks like useSearchParams; key for main entry point and demo components.

- **web/src/app/usage/page.tsx**: Usage dashboard page (/usage route); handles user session, queries for data, renders cards/skeletons; illustrates authenticated route with Stripe integration and query management.

- **web/src/app/onboard/page.tsx**: Onboarding page (/onboard route); server-side auth checks, redirects, and DB interactions; useful for protected route patterns with search params handling (e.g., auth_code).

- **web/src/components/navbar/navbar.tsx**: Navbar component; renders dynamic links based on session (e.g., /docs, /pricing, /usage, /login); central navigation hub with dropdown for mobile/small screens.

These files reveal Next.js App Router structure: pages in /app define routes (e.g., /page.tsx = /, /usage/page.tsx = /usage); layout.tsx wraps all; Navbar drives user navigation. Focus on /app for route discovery, components/ for reusable nav/UI.

import { sql } from 'drizzle-orm'
import {
  boolean,
  index,
  integer,
  jsonb,
  numeric,
  pgEnum,
  pgTable,
  primaryKey,
  text,
  timestamp,
} from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core'

import { GrantTypeValues } from '../types/grant'
import { ReferralStatusValues } from '../types/referral'

import type { SQL } from 'drizzle-orm'
import type { AdapterAccount } from 'next-auth/adapters'

export const ReferralStatus = pgEnum('referral_status', [
  ReferralStatusValues[0],
  ...ReferralStatusValues.slice(1),
])

export const apiKeyTypeEnum = pgEnum('api_key_type', [
  'anthropic',
  'gemini',
  'openai',
])

export const grantTypeEnum = pgEnum('grant_type', [
  GrantTypeValues[0],
  ...GrantTypeValues.slice(1),
])
export type GrantType = (typeof grantTypeEnum.enumValues)[number]

export const user = pgTable('user', {
  id: text('id')
    .primaryKey()
    .$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
  name: text('name'),
  email: text('email').unique().notNull(),
  password: text('password'),
  emailVerified: timestamp('emailVerified', { mode: 'date' }),
  image: text('image'),
  stripe_customer_id: text('stripe_customer_id').unique(),
  stripe_price_id: text('stripe_price_id'),
  next_quota_reset: timestamp('next_quota_reset', { mode: 'date' }).default(
    sql<Date>`now() + INTERVAL '1 month'`,
  ),
  created_at: timestamp('created_at', { mode: 'date' }).notNull().defaultNow(),
  referral_code: text('referral_code')
    .unique()
    .default(sql`'ref-' || gen_random_uuid()`),
  referral_limit: integer('referral_limit').notNull().default(5),
  discord_id: text('discord_id').unique(),
  handle: text('handle').unique(),
  auto_topup_enabled: boolean('auto_topup_enabled').notNull().default(false),
  auto_topup_threshold: integer('auto_topup_threshold'),
  auto_topup_amount: integer('auto_topup_amount'),
})

export const account = pgTable(
  'account',
  {
    userId: text('userId')
      .notNull()
      .references(() => user.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
    type: text('type').$type<AdapterAccount['type']>().notNull(),
    provider: text('provider').notNull(),
    providerAccountId: text('providerAccountId').notNull(),
    refresh_token: text('refresh_token'),
    access_token: text('access_token'),
    expires_at: integer('expires_at'),
    token_type: text('token_type'),
    scope: text('scope'),
    id_token: text('id_token'),
    session_state: text('session_state'),
  },
  (account) => [
    primaryKey({
      columns: [account.provider, account.providerAccountId],
    }),
  ],
)

export const creditLedger = pgTable(
  'credit_ledger',
  {
    operation_id: text('operation_id').primaryKey(),
    user_id: text('user_id')
      .notNull()
      .references(() => user.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
    principal: integer('principal').notNull(),
    balance: integer('balance').notNull(),
    type: grantTypeEnum('type').notNull(),
    description: text('description'),
    priority: integer('priority').notNull(),
    expires_at: timestamp('expires_at', { mode: 'date', withTimezone: true }),
    created_at: timestamp('created_at', { mode: 'date', withTimezone: true })
      .notNull()
      .defaultNow(),
    org_id: text('org_id').references(() => org.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  },
  (table) => ({
    idx_credit_ledger_active_balance: index('idx_credit_ledger_active_balance')
      .on(
        table.user_id,
        table.balance,
        table.expires_at,
        table.priority,
        table.created_at,
      )
      .where(sql`${table.balance} != 0 AND ${table.expires_at} IS NULL`),
    idx_credit_ledger_org: index('idx_credit_ledger_org').on(table.org_id),
  }),
)

export const syncFailure = pgTable(
  'sync_failure',
  {
    id: text('id').primaryKey(),
    provider: text('provider').notNull(),
    created_at: timestamp('created_at', {
      mode: 'date',
      withTimezone: true,
    })
      .notNull()
      .defaultNow(),
    last_attempt_at: timestamp('last_attempt_at', {
      mode: 'date',
      withTimezone: true,
    })
      .notNull()
      .defaultNow(),
    retry_count: integer('retry_count').notNull().default(1),
    last_error: text('last_error').notNull(),

  (table) => ({
    idx_sync_failure_retry: index('idx_sync_failure_retry')
      .on(table.retry_count, table.last_attempt_at)
      .where(sql`${table.retry_count} < 5`),
  }),
)

    created_at: timestamp('created_at', { mode: 'date' })

      .defaultNow(),
    completed_at: timestamp('completed_at', { mode: 'date' }),

  (table) => [primaryKey({ columns: [table.referrer_id, table.referred_id] })],

export const fingerprint = pgTable('fingerprint', {
  id: text('id').primaryKey(),
  sig_hash: text('sig_hash'),
  created_at: timestamp('created_at', { mode: 'date' }).notNull().defaultNow(),
})

export const message = pgTable(
  'message',
  {
    id: text('id').primaryKey(),
    finished_at: timestamp('finished_at', { mode: 'date' }).notNull(),
    client_id: text('client_id').notNull(),
    client_request_id: text('client_request_id').notNull(),
    model: text('model').notNull(),
    request: jsonb('request').notNull(),
    lastMessage: jsonb('last_message').generatedAlwaysAs(

    response: jsonb('response').notNull(),
    input_tokens: integer('input_tokens').notNull().default(0),

    cache_read_input_tokens: integer('cache_read_input_tokens')
      .notNull()
      .default(0),

    latency_ms: integer('latency_ms'),
    user_id: text('user_id').references(() => user.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
    fingerprint_id: text('fingerprint_id')
      .references(() => fingerprint.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' })
      .notNull(),
    org_id: text('org_id').references(() => org.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
    repo_url: text('repo_url'),
  },
  (table) => [
    index('message_fingerprint_id_idx').on(table.fingerprint_id),
    index('message_user_id_idx').on(table.user_id),
    index('message_finished_at_user_id_idx').on(
      table.finished_at,
      table.user_id,
    ),
    index('message_org_id_idx').on(table.org_id),
    index('message_org_id_finished_at_idx').on(table.org_id, table.finished_at),
  ],
)

export const session = pgTable('session', {

  userId: text('userId')
    .notNull()

  fingerprint_id: text('fingerprint_id').references(() => fingerprint.id),

  (vt) => [primaryKey({ columns: [vt.identifier, vt.token] })],

export const encryptedApiKeys = pgTable(

    user_id: text('user_id')
      .notNull()
      .references(() => user.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
    type: apiKeyTypeEnum('type').notNull(),
    api_key: text('api_key').notNull(),
  },
  (table) => ({
    pk: primaryKey({ columns: [table.user_id, table.type] }),

// Organization tables
export const orgRoleEnum = pgEnum('org_role', ['owner', 'admin', 'member'])

export const org = pgTable('org', {
  id: text('id')

### Relevant Files for API Routes Returning Lists with Pagination/Filtering

While the search did not yield exact matches with pagination/filtering, the following files provide patterns for authenticated GET API routes that return lists of data from the database (using Drizzle ORM and Next.js). These can serve as templates for adding pagination (e.g., via query params like `limit`/`offset`) and filtering (e.g., via `where` clauses).

- **web/src/app/api/orgs/route.ts**: GET endpoint lists user organizations with computed counts (members/repos); useful for pattern of joining tables and returning paginatable entity lists (extend with `skip`/`take` for pagination).
- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/members/route.ts**: GET lists org members with user details; shows inner joins for enriched lists, ideal base for filtered/paginated user queries.
- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/invitations/route.ts**: GET lists pending org invitations; demonstrates filtering by status (`isNull`), adaptable for date/range filters and pagination.
- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/publishers/route.ts**: GET lists org publishers with agent counts; pattern for async enrichment of list items, extendable for search/filtering on metadata.
- **web/src/app/api/api-keys/route.ts**: GET lists user's API key types (simple query); minimal example for secured list retrieval, easy to add pagination for larger datasets.

### Relevant Files for API Routes Joining Multiple Database Tables

- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/analytics/route.ts**: API route for org analytics; joins `message` (usage data) and `user` tables to aggregate top users by credits; demonstrates GROUP BY, SUM, and INNER JOIN for reporting patterns.

- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/members/route.ts**: API route for org members; joins `orgMember`, `user`, and `org` tables to fetch and validate memberships; shows INNER JOIN with AND conditions for permission checks and transactions.

- **web/src/app/api/admin/orgs/export/route.ts**: Admin API route for org export; joins `org` and `user` tables to include owner details in CSV output; illustrates simple INNER JOIN for data export with ordering.

- **web/src/app/api/publishers/route.ts**: API route for publishers; complex joins across `publisher`, `org`, `orgMember`, and `agentConfig` tables with OR/AND for access control and counts; useful for multi-table queries with permissions.

These routes exemplify patterns like authentication checks before joins, error handling, and Drizzle ORM usage for relational queries in Next.js API handlers. For schema context (to understand joinable tables), see **common/src/db/schema.ts**.

### Error Handling Patterns in API Routes

- **web/src/app/api/user/auto-topup/route.ts**: Demonstrates Zod validation errors (400 with issues), conditional validation (400), unauthorized (401), and generic try-catch (500) in a POST route for user settings.
- **web/src/app/api/stripe/buy-credits/route.ts**: Shows JSON parsing errors (400), schema validation (400), user auth checks (401/400), Stripe API errors (500 with logging), and fallback handling in a payment POST route.
- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/settings/route.ts**: Illustrates permission checks (403), missing resource (404), auth failures (401), and broad try-catch (500) across GET/PATCH/DELETE for org management.
- **web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/invitations/route.ts**: Handles duplicates (409), permissions (403), auth (401), and database errors (500) in GET/POST for invitation flows.
- **web/src/app/api/referrals/route.ts**: Covers schema parsing (400), auth/session validation (401), and query errors (500) in GET/POST for referral redemption, including fallback auth flows.

These files showcase consistent Next.js patterns: early auth/permission checks, validation with Zod, status-specific NextResponse.json, and top-level try-catch for resilience.

### Relevant Files for Pages Using React Query with Loading States and Error Handling

**web/src/app/usage/page.tsx**  
Client-side page using `useQuery` to fetch usage data; implements loading via `UsageDisplaySkeleton` and `BuyCreditsSkeleton` components, error via dedicated error card with toast notifications. Useful for patterns in authenticated data fetching, conditional rendering, and user state integration.

**web/src/hooks/use-user-profile.ts**  
Custom hook with `useQuery` for profile data; handles errors via thrown exceptions, caching, and localStorage fallback. Useful as a reusable pattern for query-based hooks with staleTime and initialData for loading optimization.

**web/src/hooks/use-org-auto-topup.ts**  
Hook combining `useQuery` and `useMutation` for org settings; manages loading via `isLoadingSettings`, errors via toast and rollback. Useful for complex state management patterns with debounced mutations and validation in org contexts.

**web/src/components/organization/credit-monitor.tsx**  
Component using multiple `useQuery` calls for credit status and settings; renders skeletons during `isLoading`, errors with fallback UI. Useful for dashboard-style patterns with progress bars, refetching, and conditional banners tied to query states.

These files demonstrate React Query integration for pages/components, emphasizing skeletons for loading UX and toast-based error recovery, aligning with UI patterns for robust data handling in authenticated apps.

### Relevant Files for Framer Motion Animations in UI Components

- **web/src/components/ui/landing/animated-element.tsx**: Core reusable component for fade, slide, and scale animations using `motion.div`; useful for understanding basic motion variants and viewport triggers in landing page elements.

Looking at the database schema and requirements, here are key considerations for TypeScript interfaces:

## Database Schema Analysis

From `common/src/db/schema.ts`:
- **publisher table**: `id` (text), `name`, `email`, `verified` (boolean), `bio`, `avatar_url`, `user_id`, `org_id`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`
- **agentConfig table**: `id`, `version`, `publisher_id`, `data` (jsonb), `created_at`, `updated_at`, plus computed `major`, `minor`, `patch`
- The `data` field contains all agent details as JSON

## Interface Design Considerations

### 1. **Agent Interface**
The agent data comes from the `data` jsonb field. Based on the agent publishing route, this includes:
- `id`: Agent identifier
- `version`: Semantic version string
- `publisher`: Publisher ID
- `displayName`: Human-readable name
- `description`: Agent description
- Likely `tags`: Array of strings for categorization
- Other fields in the dynamic agent template (subagents, tools, etc.)

**Key insight**: We need both the database row metadata AND the parsed JSON data. Suggests two approaches:
1. Single interface combining both
2. Separate interfaces (AgentConfig DB row + AgentData from JSON)

**Recommendation**: Flatten for frontend simplicity. The API should parse and merge.

### 2. **Publisher Interface**
Straightforward from schema:
- `id`, `name`, `verified`, `bio`, `avatar_url`
- Optional: `email` (privacy consideration - probably omit)
- Don't need `user_id`, `org_id`, `created_by` on frontend

### 3. **UsageMetrics Interface**
These are **mock** metrics, not from DB:
- `usage_count`: number (how many times invoked)
- `total_spent`: number (total credits spent)
- `avg_cost_per_invocation`: number (credits per use)
- `avg_response_time`: number (milliseconds or seconds)

**Consideration**: Units matter. Document in interface or use explicit naming (`avg_response_time_ms`).

## Edge Cases & Issues

1. **Agent data parsing**: The `data` jsonb field might not have consistent shape. Need safe parsing with defaults.

2. **Version handling**: Should we show full semantic version or just major.minor? The route returns latest version per agent ID, but multiple versions exist in DB.

3. **Nullable fields**: `bio`, `avatar_url`, `description`, `tags` might be null/undefined. Interfaces should reflect optionality.

4. **Publisher ownership**: Agents can be owned by users OR orgs. The joined publisher data should handle both cases transparently.

5. **Display name vs ID**: Agent `id` is system identifier, `displayName` is user-facing. Both needed? ID for routing, displayName for UI.

## Proposed Structure

```typescript
// Frontend display interface (what API returns)
interface AgentStoreItem {
  // Agent info (flattened from DB + data JSON)
  id: string
  version: string
  displayName: string
  description: string | null
  tags: string[]
  
  // Publisher info (from join)
  publisher: {
    id: string
    name: string
    verified: boolean
    avatar_url: string | null
  }
  
  // Mock metrics
  metrics: {
    usage_count: number
    total_spent: number // in credits
    avg_cost_per_invocation: number // in credits
    avg_response_time: number // in milliseconds
  }
  
  // Metadata
  created_at: string // ISO date string
}

// Alternative: Separate concerns
interface Agent {
  id: string
  version: string
  displayName: string
  description?: string
  tags: string[]
  publisherId: string
  createdAt: Date
}

interface Publisher {
  id: string
  name: string
  verified: boolean
  avatarUrl?: string
}

interface UsageMetrics {
  usageCount: number
  totalSpent: number
  avgCostPerInvocation: number
  avgResponseTimeMs: number
}
```

## Additional Context Needed

Would be helpful to:

## Recommendations

2. **Nested publisher object** - keeps related data together, easier to pass to PublisherBadge component

# Search and Filter Logic: Client vs Server-Side

## Key Considerations

**Dataset Size & Performance**
- Spec limits to 100 agents max per request
- 100 items is small enough for client-side filtering with negligible performance impact
- Server-side filtering makes sense for large datasets (1000s+), but adds complexity here
- Client-side allows instant filtering without network roundtrips

**User Experience**
- Search should feel instant - client-side filtering provides immediate feedback as user types
- No loading states or delays between filter changes improves UX significantly
- Sorting can happen instantly on client without re-fetching

**API Design Patterns**
- Looking at existing codebase patterns (usage page, orgs page), most filtering is client-side on smaller datasets
- `/api/orgs` returns full list, filtering happens in component
- Only pagination-heavy routes do server-side filtering (which we don't need here)

**Search Scope**
- Need to search across: agent name, description, tags
- Tags are in JSON data field - easier to parse once client-side than repeatedly server-side
- Fuzzy matching or partial matches easier to implement/iterate on client-side

**Sort Options**
- 'Most Used', 'Newest', 'Name', 'Total Spent'
- Some sorts depend on mock metrics generated server-side
- Can sort entire dataset client-side after initial fetch

## Recommended Approach

**Client-Side Filtering & Sorting**
1. API returns all agents (max 100) with all data pre-computed
2. React component maintains local state for search term and sort option
3. useMemo hook computes filtered/sorted results from full dataset
4. Instant updates as user types or changes sort

**Why This Works Best Here:**
- Dataset small enough (100 max)
- No pagination needed
- Better UX with instant feedback
- Simpler implementation - no query params, no API complexity
- Follows existing patterns in codebase
- Easy to add advanced filters later (by tag, verified publishers, etc.)

**Trade-offs:**
- Fetches all data upfront (but 100 agents is ~50-100KB, trivial)
- Can't reduce initial load time with server filtering (but React Query caching helps)
- Mock metrics must be deterministic (addressed in separate question)

## Implementation Pattern

```typescript
// In component
const [searchTerm, setSearchTerm] = useState('')
const [sortBy, setSortBy] = useState('newest')

const { data: agents } = useQuery(['agents'], fetchAgents)

const filteredAndSorted = useMemo(() => {
  let result = agents || []
  
  // Filter by search
  if (searchTerm) {
    result = result.filter(agent => 
      agent.name.toLowerCase().includes(searchTerm.toLowerCase()) ||
      agent.description.toLowerCase().includes(searchTerm.toLowerCase()) ||
      agent.tags.some(tag => tag.toLowerCase().includes(searchTerm.toLowerCase()))
    )
  }
  
  // Sort
  result = [...result].sort((a, b) => {
    switch(sortBy) {
      case 'mostUsed': return b.usage_count - a.usage_count
      case 'newest': return b.created_at - a.created_at
      case 'name': return a.name.localeCompare(b.name)
      case 'totalSpent': return b.total_spent - a.total_spent
    }
  })
  
  return result
}, [agents, searchTerm, sortBy])
```

**Edge Cases to Handle:**
- Empty search results - show helpful message
- No agents in system - show empty state
- Case-insensitive search
- Trim whitespace from search input
- Debouncing not needed (useMemo is fast enough)

## Alternative: Hybrid Approach

Could do server-side sorting but client-side search, but adds complexity without benefit given small dataset. Only worth it if we expect dataset to grow beyond 500+ items.

# Thinking: Number and Currency Formatting Approach

## Core Considerations

**1. Native vs. Library Approach**
- `Intl.NumberFormat` is the modern standard (built-in, zero dependencies, locale-aware)
- Already validated by researcher-docs as best practice
- No need for external libraries like `numeral.js` or `accounting.js`

**2. Reusability Requirements**
- Need utility functions in a shared location (likely `web/src/lib/utils.ts` or new `web/src/lib/formatters.ts`)
- Should handle: compact notation (1K, 1M), currency ($1,234.56), and precision
- TypeScript interfaces for options to ensure type safety

**3. Key Decisions**

**Where to place utilities?**
- Option A: Extend existing `web/src/lib/utils.ts` (pros: centralized, cons: cluttered)
- Option B: Create new `web/src/lib/formatters.ts` (pros: focused, cons: another file)
- **Recommendation**: New file `formatters.ts` for clarity and future growth

**Locale handling?**
- Use `navigator.language` as default for browser locale detection
- Allow override via optional `locale` parameter
- For this feature, `'en-US'` is likely sufficient (US-based product)

**Compact notation specifics?**
- `Intl.NumberFormat` with `notation: 'compact'` auto-handles K/M/B
- Example: `1234` → `"1.2K"`, `1234567` → `"1.2M"`
- `compactDisplay: 'short'` for brevity (vs 'long' which gives "1.2 thousand")

**Currency formatting specifics?**
- Need `style: 'currency'` + `currency: 'USD'` (or dynamic)
- `minimumFractionDigits: 2` ensures cents display (e.g., `$1,234.00`)
- Handle negative values (e.g., `-$50.00` for refunds/credits)

**Edge cases to handle:**
- Zero values: `0` → `"0"` or `"$0.00"`
- Very large numbers: `1e15` → `"1000T"` (trillions)
- Very small numbers: `0.001` → `"0"` with compact (might need threshold)
- Negative numbers: `-1000` → `"-1K"`
- `null`/`undefined` inputs: Return fallback like `"—"` or `"N/A"`

## Proposed Structure

**Utility Functions:**
```typescript
// web/src/lib/formatters.ts

export const formatCompactNumber = (
  value: number | null | undefined,
  locale = 'en-US'
): string => {
  if (value == null) return '—';
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {
    notation: 'compact',
    compactDisplay: 'short',
    maximumFractionDigits: 1
  }).format(value);
};

export const formatCurrency = (
  value: number | null | undefined,
  currency = 'USD',
  locale = 'en-US'
): string => {
  if (value == null) return '—';
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {
    style: 'currency',
    currency,
    minimumFractionDigits: 2,
    maximumFractionDigits: 2
  }).format(value);
};
```

**Performance Optimization:**
- **Don't** create formatter instances in loops/renders
- **Do** use `useMemo` in React components if formatting in render
- **Consider** caching formatters if used repeatedly (though overhead is minimal)

**Testing Insights:**
- Unit tests for edge cases (0, negative, null, very large)
- Locale tests (ensure `en-US` vs `de-DE` work differently if needed)
- Integration tests in components (e.g., agent card displays "1.2K" correctly)

**Alternative Considerations:**
- For precise decimal handling (e.g., financial calculations), use integers (cents) internally, format only for display
- If global i18n is needed later, integrate with `react-i18next` context
- For custom formats (e.g., "1.23K users" with suffix), extend with template strings

**Integration with Existing Code:**
- Existing `web/src/lib/utils.ts` has `cn()` for classNames and `clamp()` for numbers
- Pattern matches: small, focused utilities
- Can import in components like: `import { formatCompactNumber, formatCurrency } from '@/lib/formatters'`

**Potential Issues:**
- Browser compatibility: `Intl.NumberFormat` with `notation: 'compact'` requires ES2020+ (all modern browsers, but check if targeting older)
- SSR: `navigator.language` is client-only; use default or pass locale from server
- Decimal precision: `maximumFractionDigits: 1` means `1234` → `"1.2K"`, but `1234567` → `"1.2M"` (might want 0 for whole numbers)

**Recommendation for Agent Store:**
- Use `formatCompactNumber` for usage_count (e.g., "1.2K invocations")
- Use `formatCurrency` for total_spent, avg_cost_per_invocation (e.g., "$1,234.56", "$0.05")
- For avg_response_time, use plain number with unit (e.g., "1.2s" manually or `${value.toFixed(1)}s`)

This approach balances simplicity, performance, and maintainability while leveraging native APIs.

# Mock Usage Metrics Generation Analysis

## Core Question
Should mock metrics be random, deterministic (based on agent ID), or follow patterns?

## Key Considerations

### 1. **Purpose of Mock Data**
- **Demo/Testing**: If this is placeholder data until real metrics exist, consistency matters less
- **User Trust**: Inconsistent/obviously fake data erodes confidence
- **Future Migration**: Will real metrics eventually replace these? Design for easy swap

### 2. **Deterministic vs Random**

**Deterministic (Hash-based on agent ID):**
- ✅ Consistent across page reloads (better UX)
- ✅ Predictable for testing/debugging
- ✅ Avoids confusing users with changing numbers
- ✅ Can create realistic distributions (newer agents = lower usage)
- ❌ Pattern might be detectable if users check multiple times

**Pure Random:**
- ✅ Appears more "real" superficially
- ❌ Confusing when numbers change on reload
- ❌ Harder to test
- ❌ Can't correlate with agent characteristics (age, publisher, etc.)

**Hybrid Approach:**
- Use deterministic seed based on `agent_id + publisher_id`
- Add small random variance (±10%) to avoid obvious patterns
- Cache in DB or response for session consistency

### 3. **Realistic Patterns to Model**

From analyzing the schema and typical agent usage:
- **Newer agents** (recent `created_at`) → Lower usage counts
- **Verified publishers** → Higher average usage (more trust)
- **Usage correlates with age**: Linear or logarithmic growth over time
- **Cost distributions**: Most agents low cost (<$0.10/invocation), few expensive outliers
- **Response time**: Cluster around 2-5s, some fast (<1s), some slow (>10s)

### 4. **Implementation Approaches**

**Option A: Simple Hash-Based**
```typescript
// Deterministic seed from agent ID
const seed = hashCode(agentId + publisherId)
const usageCount = (seed % 10000) + 100 // 100-10,100 range
const totalSpent = usageCount * (0.01 + (seed % 50) / 1000) // $0.01-$0.05 per use
```
- Pros: Fast, no DB changes, consistent
- Cons: Distribution might not feel natural

**Option B: Time-Based Realistic**
```typescript
const ageDays = daysSince(agent.created_at)
const baseUsage = Math.log(ageDays + 1) * 50 // Logarithmic growth
const variance = hash(agentId) % 30 - 15 // ±15% variance
const usageCount = Math.floor(baseUsage * (1 + variance/100))
```
- Pros: Correlates with agent age (more realistic)
- Cons: More complex, requires `created_at` in response

**Option C: Store in DB**
```sql
-- Add columns to agent_config table
ALTER TABLE agent_config ADD mock_usage_count INTEGER;
ALTER TABLE agent_config ADD mock_total_spent INTEGER;
```
- Pros: Truly consistent, can manually curate "featured" agents
- Cons: Schema change, migration needed, not requested in spec

### 5. **Edge Cases to Handle**
- **Zero usage**: Brand new agents should show 0 or very low counts
- **Cost validation**: `total_spent ≈ usage_count × avg_cost_per_invocation` (within reason)
- **Outliers**: Include some high-usage agents for realism (top 5% >> median)
- **Response time**: Should be independent of usage (fast agents can be popular or unpopular)

### 6. **Recommendation**

**Use Option B (Time-Based Deterministic with Hash Variance)**:

**Why:**
1. **Consistency**: Same numbers on reload (good UX)
2. **Realism**: Newer agents naturally have lower usage
3. **Testability**: Deterministic but varied enough to look real
4. **No Schema Changes**: Works with current DB structure
5. **Easy Migration**: When real metrics arrive, just remove the mock logic

**Implementation Sketch:**
```typescript
function generateMockMetrics(agent: { id: string, created_at: Date, publisher_id: string }) {
  const seed = hashCode(agent.id + agent.publisher_id)
  const ageDays = Math.max(1, daysBetween(agent.created_at, new Date()))
  
  // Usage grows logarithmically with age, with variance
  const baseUsage = Math.log(ageDays + 1) * 100
  const usageVariance = (seed % 60) - 30 // ±30%
  const usage_count = Math.floor(baseUsage * (1 + usageVariance/100))
  
  // Cost per invocation: $[redacted] to $0.15 (most under $0.05)
  const costSeed = (seed * 17) % 100
  const avg_cost = 0.005 + (costSeed < 80 ? costSeed/1000 : costSeed/200)
  
  const total_spent = usage_count * avg_cost
  
  // Response time: 1-8s, cluster around 2-4s
  const timeSeed = (seed * 31) % 100
  const avg_response_time = 1 + (timeSeed < 70 ? timeSeed/25 : timeSeed/10)
  
  return { usage_count, total_spent, avg_cost_per_invocation: avg_cost, avg_response_time }
}
```

**Alternative if simplicity preferred**: Pure hash-based with wider ranges, accept less realism for easier code.

### 7. **Testing Considerations**
- Document that these are MOCK metrics in code comments
- Add flag/env var to disable mocks when real data available
- Ensure formatting functions handle edge cases (0, very large numbers)

# Common Package Knowledge

This package contains code shared between the `web` (Next.js frontend/backend) and `backend` (CLI backend) packages.

## Key Areas

- **Database (`src/db`)**: Drizzle ORM schema (`schema.ts`), configuration, and migration logic
- **Utilities (`src/util`)**: Shared helper functions
- **Types (`src/types`)**: Shared TypeScript types and interfaces
- **Constants (`src/constants`)**: Shared constant values
- **API Keys (`src/api-keys`)**: Encryption/decryption utilities for sensitive data

## API Key Encryption (`src/api-keys/crypto.ts`)

- Provides functions for encrypting/decrypting API keys (`encryptAndStoreApiKey`, `retrieveAndDecryptApiKey`, `clearApiKey`)
- **Security**: Functions require the 32-byte `API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET` from environment variables
- The secret must **never** be stored in the `common` package - calling environments retrieve it from their respective `env` files

## Database Migrations

- Schema defined in `common/src/db/schema.ts`
- Generate migrations: `bun run --cwd common db:generate`
- Apply migrations: `bun run --cwd common db:migrate`

## Credit Grant Management

Credit grants are managed in `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts`:

- Use `processAndGrantCredit` for standalone grants (handles retries and failure logging)
- Use `grantCreditOperation` for grants within a larger database transaction
- Grant types: 'free', 'referral', 'rollover', 'purchase', 'admin'
- Each type has priority level from `GRANT_PRIORITIES`
- Always include unique `operation_id` for tracking

### Credit Grant Flow

1. Create local credit grant record immediately
2. Create Stripe grant asynchronously
3. Webhook updates local grant with Stripe ID when confirmed

### Monthly Reset Flow

1. Calculate unused purchase/rollover credits
2. Create new rollover grant if needed
3. Reset usage to 0 and update `next_quota_reset`
4. Create new free/referral grants with expiration

eval_commit.spec:
The WebSocket client needs to be refactored to simplify its API and remove certain functionality:

## Action Schema Changes
Remove the `generate-commit-message` action type from the `CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA` discriminated union in the actions file. This action type should no longer be supported as a valid client action.

## WebSocketHandler Class Changes

### Constructor and Properties
- Add an `apiKey` field to the `WebSocketHandlerOptions` type as a required string property
- Add a private `apiKey` property to the `WebSocketHandler` class
- Update the constructor to accept the `apiKey` from options and store it as an instance property

### Method Changes
- Remove the public `init` method entirely from the `WebSocketHandler` class
- Add a new public `sendInput` method that:
  - Accepts a prompt action object but with certain default fields omitted (the fields that will be automatically provided)
  - Automatically merges in default values including `type: 'prompt'`, `fingerprintId: 'codebuff-sdk'`, and the stored `authToken` (using the apiKey)
  - Sends the complete action via the websocket
- Add a new public `cancelInput` method that:
  - Accepts an object with a `promptId` field
  - Sends a `cancel-user-input` action with the `authToken` set to the stored apiKey and the provided promptId
- Add a private helper method `getInputDefaultOptions` that returns an object containing the default fields that should be automatically applied to prompt actions

The goal is to simplify the client API by removing the init method, storing the API key internally, and providing convenient methods that automatically handle common default values when sending actions.

import { z } from 'zod'

import { costModes } from './constants'
import { GrantTypeValues } from './types/grant'
import { printModeEventSchema } from './types/print-mode'
import {
  SessionStateSchema,
  toolCallSchema,
  toolResultSchema,
} from './types/session-state'
import { ProjectFileContextSchema } from './util/file'

export const FileChangeSchema = z.object({
  type: z.enum(['patch', 'file']),
  path: z.string(),
  content: z.string(),
})
export type FileChange = z.infer<typeof FileChangeSchema>
export const CHANGES = z.array(FileChangeSchema)
export type FileChanges = z.infer<typeof CHANGES>

export const CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('prompt'),
    promptId: z.string(),
    prompt: z.string().or(z.undefined()),
    promptParams: z.record(z.string(), z.any()).optional(), // Additional json params.
    fingerprintId: z.string(),
    authToken: z.string().optional(),
    costMode: z.enum(costModes).optional().default('normal'),
    sessionState: SessionStateSchema,
    toolResults: z.array(toolResultSchema),
    model: z.string().optional(),
    repoUrl: z.string().optional(),
    agentId: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('read-files-response'),
    files: z.record(z.string(), z.union([z.string(), z.null()])),
    requestId: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('init'),
    fingerprintId: z.string(),
    authToken: z.string().optional(),
    fileContext: ProjectFileContextSchema,
    repoUrl: z.string().optional(),

import { z } from 'zod'

import { costModes } from './constants'
import { GrantTypeValues } from './types/grant'
import { printModeEventSchema } from './types/print-mode'
import {
  SessionStateSchema,
  toolCallSchema,
  toolResultSchema,
} from './types/session-state'
import { ProjectFileContextSchema } from './util/file'

export const FileChangeSchema = z.object({
  type: z.enum(['patch', 'file']),
  path: z.string(),
  content: z.string(),
})
export type FileChange = z.infer<typeof FileChangeSchema>
export const CHANGES = z.array(FileChangeSchema)
export type FileChanges = z.infer<typeof CHANGES>

export const CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('prompt'),
    promptId: z.string(),
    prompt: z.string().or(z.undefined()),
    promptParams: z.record(z.string(), z.any()).optional(), // Additional json params.
    fingerprintId: z.string(),
    authToken: z.string().optional(),
    costMode: z.enum(costModes).optional().default('normal'),
    sessionState: SessionStateSchema,
    toolResults: z.array(toolResultSchema),
    model: z.string().optional(),
    repoUrl: z.string().optional(),
    agentId: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('read-files-response'),
    files: z.record(z.string(), z.union([z.string(), z.null()])),
    requestId: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('init'),
    fingerprintId: z.string(),
    authToken: z.string().optional(),
    fileContext: ProjectFileContextSchema,
    repoUrl: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('generate-commit-message'),
    fingerprintId: z.string(),
    authToken: z.string().optional(),
    stagedChanges: z.string(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('tool-call-response'),
    requestId: z.string(),
    success: z.boolean(),
    result: z.any().optional(), // Tool execution result
    error: z.string().optional(), // Error message if execution failed
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('cancel-user-input'),
    authToken: z.string(),
    promptId: z.string(),
  }),
])

export type ClientAction = z.infer<typeof CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA>

export const UsageReponseSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('usage-response'),
  usage: z.number(),
  remainingBalance: z.number(),
  balanceBreakdown: z
    .record(
      z.enum([GrantTypeValues[0], ...GrantTypeValues.slice(1)]),
      z.number(),
    )
    .optional(),
  next_quota_reset: z.coerce.date().nullable(),
  autoTopupAdded: z.number().optional(),
})
export type UsageResponse = z.infer<typeof UsageReponseSchema>

export const InitResponseSchema = z
  .object({
    type: z.literal('init-response'),
    message: z.string().optional(),
    agentNames: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional(),
  })
  .merge(
    UsageReponseSchema.omit({
      type: true,
    }),
  )
export type InitResponse = z.infer<typeof InitResponseSchema>

export const MessageCostResponseSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('message-cost-response'),
  promptId: z.string(),
  credits: z.number(),
})
export type MessageCostResponse = z.infer<typeof MessageCostResponseSchema>

export const PromptResponseSchema = z.object({
  type: z.literal('prompt-response'),
  promptId: z.string(),
  sessionState: SessionStateSchema,
  toolCalls: z.array(toolCallSchema),
  toolResults: z.array(toolResultSchema),
})
export type PromptResponse = z.infer<typeof PromptResponseSchema>

export const SERVER_ACTION_SCHEMA = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('response-chunk'),
    userInputId: z.string(),
    chunk: z.union([z.string(), printModeEventSchema]),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('subagent-response-chunk'),
    userInputId: z.string(),
    agentId: z.string(),
    agentType: z.string(),
    chunk: z.string(),
    prompt: z.string().optional(),
  }),
  PromptResponseSchema,
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('read-files'),
    filePaths: z.array(z.string()),
    requestId: z.string(),
  }),
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('tool-call-request'),
    userInputId: z.string(),
    requestId: z.string(),
    toolName: z.string(),
    args: z.record(z.any()),
    timeout: z.number().optional(),
  }),
  InitResponseSchema,
  UsageReponseSchema,
  MessageCostResponseSchema,
  z.object({
    type: z.literal('action-error'),
    message: z.string(),
    error: z.string().optional(),
    remainingBalance: z.number().optional(),
  }),
  z.object({
    // The server is imminently going to shutdown, and the client should reconnect
    type: z.literal('request-reconnect'),
  }),
])

export type ServerAction = z.infer<typeof SERVER_ACTION_SCHEMA>

### Relevant Files for Actions Schemas and WebSocket Client Implementation

- **common/src/actions.ts**: Core Zod schemas for ClientAction (e.g., 'prompt', 'init') and ServerAction (e.g., 'response-chunk', 'prompt-response'); central to defining action structure and types shared across client/server.

- **common/src/websockets/websocket-schema.ts**: Defines WebSocket message schemas that embed CLIENT_ACTION_SCHEMA and SERVER_ACTION_SCHEMA; ensures actions are validated/transmitted correctly over WebSocket.

- **common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts**: Implements APIRealtimeClient class for sending ClientActions (e.g., sendAction) and subscribing to ServerActions; handles reconnection, acknowledgments, and action dispatching.

- **backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts**: Server-side handler for incoming ClientActions (e.g., onPrompt, onInit) and sending ServerActions; includes auth, usage responses, and tool/file request logic tied to action schemas.

- **npm-app/src/client.ts**: NPM client implementation using WebSocket client to send ClientActions (e.g., during user input/prompts) and process ServerActions (e.g., response chunks); manages session state and tool responses per schemas.

These files form the action schema foundation and WebSocket integration; actions.ts is the primary schema source, with others handling transmission/execution.

### WebSocket Client Implementation Analysis

- **common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts**: Core APIRealtimeClient class for WebSocket connection management, reconnection, message sending/receiving, and subscriptions; essential for client-side real-time communication with the server.

- **npm-app/src/client.ts**: Initializes and integrates APIRealtimeClient with the CLI app, handles subscriptions to server actions (e.g., tool calls, usage updates), and manages session state over WebSocket; key for app-level WebSocket usage.

- **common/src/websockets/websocket-schema.ts**: Zod schemas for ClientMessage and ServerMessage types (including actions); defines structure for WebSocket payloads, ensuring type-safe communication between client and server.

### Relevant Files Analysis

- **npm-app/src/client.ts**: Core npm client implementation; subscribes to 'npm-version-status' action for version checks/updates and generates commit messages via 'generate-commit-message' action over WebSocket. Essential for understanding client-side handling of these features in the context of actions and WS communication.

- **common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts**: Shared WebSocket client class; provides `sendAction` and subscription mechanisms used by npm client for 'npm-version-status' and commit-related actions. Useful for tracing WS action flow.

- **backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts**: Backend handler for client actions; processes 'generate-commit-message' requests and sends 'npm-version-status' responses. Key for server-side integration with npm client's WS subscriptions.

These files directly tie into the overall goal by showing action schemas ('npm-version-status', 'commit-message-response') and WS client-server interplay for npm client features. Other results (e.g., analytics.ts, cli.ts) are tangential and less relevant.

Looking at the SDK structure and the existing `APIRealtimeClient` implementation, here are key insights for designing `WebSocketHandler`:

## Core Design Principles

1. **Mirror existing patterns**: The SDK's `WebSocketHandler` should be a lightweight wrapper around `APIRealtimeClient` since that's the battle-tested implementation. Don't reinvent the wheel.

2. **Event-driven architecture**: Match the existing callback pattern but make it more flexible:
   - Constructor should accept optional callbacks: `onOpen`, `onMessage`, `onClose`, `onError`
   - `onError` must match the new signature: `(event: WebSocket.ErrorEvent) => void`
   - `onMessage` should receive parsed `ServerAction` objects, not raw data

3. **Method surface area**:
   - `connect(url: string)`: Establish connection (async, returns Promise)
   - `send(message: any)`: Send arbitrary messages
   - `sendAction(action: ClientAction)`: Type-safe action sending
   - `close()`: Clean shutdown
   - `subscribe(actionType, callback)`: Listen to specific server actions
   - `runNewChat(prompt, options)`: High-level API for common use case

4. **URL management**: The class needs smart defaults:
   - Detect `NODE_ENV` or similar env var for dev vs prod
   - Dev: `ws://localhost:3000` (or configurable port)
   - Prod: `wss://api.codebuff.com` or similar
   - Allow explicit URL override in `connect()`

5. **Type safety concerns**:
   - Inline parameter types per the requirement (no imports from types.ts)
   - This means duplicating some type definitions, which is acceptable for SDK simplicity
   - Use JSDoc comments to document inline types

6. **Authentication handling**:
   - `runNewChat` needs `cwd` and optionally `authToken` or `fingerprintId`
   - Should read from `process.env.CODEBUFF_API_KEY` by default
   - Constructor should accept auth options

7. **State management**:
   - Track connection state (connecting, open, closed)
   - Expose `readyState` getter
   - Handle reconnection logic (may delegate to APIRealtimeClient)

## Potential Issues

- **Duplication risk**: If WebSocketHandler wraps APIRealtimeClient, we're creating two similar classes. Consider if WebSocketHandler should just re-export a configured APIRealtimeClient instance instead.

- **Breaking changes**: The inline type requirement means SDK consumers can't import types from `@codebuff/sdk/types` anymore. This is intentional for simplification but could break existing code.

- **Environment detection fragility**: `process.env.NODE_ENV` isn't always set. Consider falling back to other heuristics or requiring explicit environment specification.

- **Error handling cascade**: With the new `onError` signature, errors need to bubble up properly through the WebSocket stack to provide useful debugging info.

## Alternative Approaches

**Option A (Minimal)**: Make `WebSocketHandler` a thin facade that just configures and returns an `APIRealtimeClient` instance with environment-aware defaults.

**Option B (Comprehensive)**: Build a full standalone implementation that doesn't depend on `APIRealtimeClient`, giving SDK users a cleaner API without common module dependencies.

**Recommendation**: Option A is better because:
- Reduces duplication
- Leverages tested reconnection logic
- Easier to maintain consistency
- SDK remains lightweight

The key is making the SDK's `WebSocketHandler` feel like a "batteries included" version of the lower-level `APIRealtimeClient`.

## Key Insights:

**1. Current Usage Pattern**
- The constructor takes `onError: () => void` 
- It's called without arguments: `this.onError()`
- The actual error event is available in `ws.onerror = (ev) => {...}` but not passed through

**2. Backward Compatibility Concerns**
- Existing clients pass callbacks expecting no parameters
- Changing to require a parameter could break existing code
- TypeScript will catch this at compile time, but runtime behavior matters

**3. Migration Strategies**

**Option A: Breaking Change (Simplest)**
- Just change the signature
- TypeScript users get compile errors and must update
- Runtime: old callbacks will ignore the parameter (safe in JS)
- Risk: Low for TypeScript users, medium for JS users who won't get warnings

**Option B: Optional Parameter**
- Make it `(event?: WebSocket.ErrorEvent) => void`
- Maintains backward compatibility
- Old code works, new code can access event
- Risk: Very low, cleanest migration path

**Option C: Function Overloading**
- Support both signatures via overloading
- Check callback.length to determine which version to call
- Complex implementation, unclear benefit

**Option D: Deprecation Period**
- Keep old signature, add new callback property
- Mark old one deprecated
- Remove in next major version
- Risk: Lowest, but adds technical debt

**4. Recommendation: Option B (Optional Parameter)**

Reasoning:
- JavaScript functions ignore extra parameters by default
- Old callbacks like `() => { console.log('error') }` will work fine when called with `callback(event)`
- New callbacks can be `(event) => { console.log(event.message) }`
- TypeScript properly represents both use cases
- No runtime breaking changes
- Clean, simple implementation

**5. Implementation Details**
- Change constructor: `onError: (event?: WebSocket.ErrorEvent) => void`
- Change property: `onError: (event?: WebSocket.ErrorEvent) => void`
- Change call site: `this.onError(ev)` (always pass event)
- Old code: ignores parameter, continues working
- New code: can access error details

**6. Documentation Needed**
- JSDoc comment explaining the parameter is now available
- Migration guide mentioning the enhancement
- No breaking change announcement needed

**7. Testing Considerations**
- Test with callback that takes no parameters (backward compat)
- Test with callback that uses the event parameter (new functionality)
- Verify TypeScript compilation for both patterns

This approach minimizes risk while providing the enhancement requested.

/**
 * WebSocketHandler provides direct WebSocket-based communication with the Codebuff backend.
 * 
 * This class handles WebSocket connections, message passing, and provides high-level APIs
 * for running AI-powered coding tasks. Unlike CodebuffClient which uses binary execution,
 * WebSocketHandler communicates directly with the backend via WebSocket protocol.
 * 
 * Note: Reconnection logic is the consumer's responsibility. If the connection is lost,
 * you will need to call connect() again and re-establish any subscriptions.
 * 
 * @example
 * const handler = new WebSocketHandler({
 *   cwd: '/path/to/project',
 *   fingerprintId: 'user-123',
 *   onError: (event) => console.error('WebSocket error:', event)
 * })
 * 
 * await handler.connect()
 * await handler.runNewChat('Implement user authentication', {
 *   agent: 'buffy',
 *   handleEvent: (event) => console.log(event)
 * })
 */
export class WebSocketHandler {
  private ws: WebSocket | null = null
  private cwd: string
  private fingerprintId: string
  private onOpenCallback?: () => void
  private onMessageCallback?: (data: any) => void
  private onCloseCallback?: () => void
  private onErrorCallback?: (event?: WebSocket.ErrorEvent) => void
  private subscribers: Map<ServerAction['type'], ((action: ServerAction) => void)[]> = new Map()
  private txid = 0
  private txns: Map<number, { resolve: () => void; reject: (err: Error) => void }> = new Map()

  constructor(options: WebSocketHandlerOptions) {
    this.cwd = options.cwd
    this.fingerprintId = options.fingerprintId || `sdk-user-${Date.now()}`
    this.onOpenCallback = options.onOpen
    this.onMessageCallback = options.onMessage
    this.onCloseCallback = options.onClose
    this.onErrorCallback = options.onError
  }

+import { WebSocket } from 'ws'
+
+import { API_KEY_ENV_VAR } from '../../common/src/constants'
+import { getInitialSessionState } from '../../common/src/types/session-state'
+
+import type { ClientAction, ServerAction } from '../../common/src/actions'
+import type { AgentTemplateType } from '../../common/src/types/session-state'
+import type { PrintModeEvent } from '../../common/src/types/print-mode'
+import type { ProjectFileContext } from '../../common/src/util/file'
+
+const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'
+const baseUrl = isDev ? 'ws://localhost:3000' : 'wss://api.codebuff.com'
+
+type WebSocketHandlerOptions = {
+  cwd: string
+  fingerprintId?: string
+  onOpen?: () => void
+  onMessage?: (data: any) => void
+  onClose?: () => void
+  onError?: (event?: WebSocket.ErrorEvent) => void
+}
+
+/**
+ * WebSocketHandler provides direct WebSocket-based communication with the Codebuff backend.
+ * 
+ * This class handles WebSocket connections, message passing, and provides high-level APIs
+ * for running AI-powered coding tasks. Unlike CodebuffClient which uses binary execution,
+ * WebSocketHandler communicates directly with the backend via WebSocket protocol.
+ * 
+ * Note: Reconnection logic is the consumer's responsibility. If the connection is lost,
+ * you will need to call connect() again and re-establish any subscriptions.
+ * 
+ * @example
+ * const handler = new WebSocketHandler({
+ *   cwd: '/path/to/project',
+ *   fingerprintId: 'user-123',
+ *   onError: (event) => console.error('WebSocket error:', event)
+ * })
+ * 
+ * await handler.connect()
+ * await handler.runNewChat('Implement user authentication', {
+ *   agent: 'buffy',
+ *   handleEvent: (event) => console.log(event)
+ * })
+ */
+export class WebSocketHandler {
+  private ws: WebSocket | null = null
+  private cwd: string
+  private fingerprintId: string
+  private onOpenCallback?: () => void
+  private onMessageCallback?: (data: any) => void
+  private onCloseCallback?: () => void
+  private onErrorCallback?: (event?: WebSocket.ErrorEvent) => void
+  private subscribers: Map<ServerAction['type'], ((action: ServerAction) => void)[]> = new Map()
+  private txid = 0
+  private txns: Map<number, { resolve: () => void; reject: (err: Error) => void }> = new Map()
+
+  constructor(options: WebSocketHandlerOptions) {
+    this.cwd = options.cwd
+    this.fingerprintId = options.fingerprintId || `sdk-user-${Date.now()}`
+    this.onOpenCallback = options.onOpen
+    this.onMessageCallback = options.onMessage
+    this.onCloseCallback = options.onClose
+    this.onErrorCallback = options.onError
+  }
+
+  public async connect(url?: string): Promise<void> {
+    const wsUrl = url || baseUrl
+    
+    return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
+      this.ws = new WebSocket(wsUrl)
+
+      this.ws.onopen = () => {
+        if (this.onOpenCallback) {
+          this.onOpenCallback()
+        }
+        resolve()
+      }
+
+      this.ws.onmessage = (event) => {
+        try {
+          const data = JSON.parse(event.data as string)
+          
+          if (this.onMessageCallback) {
+            this.onMessageCallback(data)
+          }
+
+          if (data.type === 'action') {
+            const action = data.data as ServerAction
+            const subscribers = this.subscribers.get(action.type) || []
+            for (const callback of subscribers) {
+              callback(action)
+            }
+          }
+
+          if (data.type === 'ack' && data.txid != null) {
+            const txn = this.txns.get(data.txid)
+            if (txn) {
+              if (data.error) {
+                txn.reject(new Error(data.error))
+              } else {
+                txn.resolve()
+              }
+              this.txns.delete(data.txid)
+            }
+          }
+        } catch (error) {
+          console.error('Error parsing WebSocket message:', error)
+        }
+      }
+
+      this.ws.onerror = (event) => {
+        if (this.onErrorCallback) {
+          this.onErrorCallback(event as WebSocket.ErrorEvent)
+        }
+        reject(new Error('WebSocket connection error'))
+      }
+
+      this.ws.onclose = () => {
+        if (this.onCloseCallback) {
+          this.onCloseCallback()
+        }
+      }
+    })
+  }
+
+  public send(message: any): Promise<void> {
+    if (!this.ws || this.ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) {
+      return Promise.reject(new Error('WebSocket is not connected'))
+    }
+
+    return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
+      const txid = this.txid++
+      this.txns.set(txid, { resolve, reject })
+      
+      this.ws!.send(JSON.stringify({ ...message, txid }))
+      
+      setTimeout(() => {
+        if (this.txns.has(txid)) {
+          this.txns.delete(txid)
+          reject(new Error('WebSocket message timeout'))
+        }
+      }, 30000)
+    })
+  }
+
+  public async sendAction(action: ClientAction): Promise<void> {
+    return this.send({ type: 'action', data: action })
+  }
+
+  public subscribe<T extends ServerAction['type']>(
+    actionType: T,
+    callback: (action: Extract<ServerAction, { type: T }>) => void
+  ): () => void {
+    const currentSubscribers = this.subscribers.get(actionType) || []
+    this.subscribers.set(actionType, [
+      ...currentSubscribers,
+      callback as (action: ServerAction) => void,
+    ])
+
+    return () => {
+      const subscribers = this.subscribers.get(actionType) || []
+      this.subscribers.set(
+        actionType,
+        subscribers.filter((cb) => cb !== callback)
+      )
+    }
+  }
+
+  public close(): void {
+    if (this.ws) {
+      this.ws.close()
+      this.ws = null
+    }
+  }
+
+  public async runNewChat(
+    prompt: string,
+    options?: {
+      cwd?: string
+      agent?: AgentTemplateType
+      params?: Record<string, any>
+      handleEvent?: (event: PrintModeEvent) => void
+    }
+  ): Promise<{ agentId: string; chatId?: string }> {
+    const cwd = options?.cwd || this.cwd
+    const agent = options?.agent || 'buffy'
+    const params = options?.params
+    const handleEvent = options?.handleEvent
+
+    if (handleEvent) {
+      this.subscribe('response-chunk', (action) => {
+        if (typeof action.chunk !== 'string') {
+          handleEvent(action.chunk)
+        }
+      })
+    }
+
+    const apiKey = process.env[API_KEY_ENV_VAR]
+    if (!apiKey) {
+      throw new Error(
+        `Codebuff API key not found. Please set the ${API_KEY_ENV_VAR} environment variable.`
+      )
+    }
+
+    const fileContext: ProjectFileContext = {
+      projectRoot: cwd,
+      cwd,
+      fileTree: [],
+      fileTokenScores: {},
+      knowledgeFiles: {},
+      agentTemplates: {},
+      gitChanges: {
+        status: '',
+        diff: '',
+        diffCached: '',
+        lastCommitMessages: '',
+      },
+      changesSinceLastChat: {},
+      shellConfigFiles: {},
+      systemInfo: {
+        platform: process.platform,
+        shell: process.env.SHELL || '',
+        nodeVersion: process.version,
+        arch: process.arch,
+        homedir: process.env.HOME || '',
+        cpus: 0,
+      },
+    }
+
+    const sessionState = getInitialSessionState(fileContext)
+
+    await this.sendAction({
+      type: 'prompt',
+      promptId: `chat-${Date.now()}`,
+      prompt,
+      promptParams: params,
+      sessionState,
+      toolResults: [],
+      fingerprintId: this.fingerprintId,
+      authToken: apiKey,
+      costMode: 'normal',
+      agentId: agent,
+    })
+
+    return {
+      agentId: agent,
+    }
+  }
+}
